title: Alteration of intracellular taurine transporter expression in CCl 4 ‐induced liver disease

sections.abstract: <jats:p> <jats:bold>Background/Aim:</jats:bold> Taurine is taken up by hepatocytes through a specific transporter (TAUT), and exerts hepatoprotection via the regulation of oxidative stress and apoptosis. Hepatic taurine levels are markedly decreased in liver disease (LD), and decreased hepatic taurine content is associated liver injury and mitochondria (Mt) abnormality. This study investigated the total, membrane and Mt TAUT expression level in LD. </jats:p> <jats:p> <jats:bold>Methods:</jats:bold> Rats were administrated CCl <jats:sub>4</jats:sub> with/out taurine for 5 or 15 weeks. The hepatic TAUT mRNA and protein expression levels were examined by RT‐PCR, Western blotting, while the Mt membrane potential (mΔΨ) by confocal microscopy. </jats:p> <jats:p> <jats:bold>Results:</jats:bold> CCl <jats:sub>4</jats:sub> administration resulted in a significant decrease in taurine concentration and mΔΨ, but the liver condition improved upon taurine administration. The Mt and cytoplasmic expressions of TAUT were significant lower in CCl <jats:sub>4</jats:sub> rats vs normal, while the TAUT mRNA expression level was unchanged. The Mt porin level was significantly reduced by CCl <jats:sub>4</jats:sub> after 15 but not 5 weeks. Taurine administration prevented the loss of TAUT in the cytoplasm but not in the Mt. </jats:p> <jats:p> <jats:bold>Conclusion:</jats:bold> The decrease in Mt TAUT level may precede the Mt abnormality in the CCl <jats:sub>4</jats:sub> ‐induced LD rat model. Therefore, the maintenance of taurine in Mt via TAUT may be one of key factors to prolong viability and function of the hepatocytes. </jats:p>
